Founded, by legend, by Cerdic and Cynric of the Gewisse, this Anglo-Saxon kingdom in southern Britain lasted from around 519 to 927 — what was it called?
Wessex: Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the south of Great Britain.
This man is the younger brother of China's current top leader, and serves as president of an international energy conservation and environmental protection association — who is he?
Xi Yuanping: Son of Xi Zhongxun, brother of Xi Jinping.
An electrical engineer who was branded a "rightist" for criticizing Mao's economic policies during the Hundred Flowers Campaign, he went on to serve as China's premier from 1998 to 2003 — who is he?
Zhu Rongji: Premier of China from 1998 to 2003. Born in Changsha, Hunan, Zhu became a member of the CCP in 1949, the same year the People's Republic of China was established.
Which of these people was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four has been around longest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Dorothea Klumpke is an astronomer. Dorothea Klumpke Roberts (August 9, 1861 in San Francisco – October 5, 1942 in San Francisco) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Eric Weinstein is a mathematician. Eric Ross Weinstein (born October 26, 1965) is an American investor and podcast host.
What is the atomic number of Unbinilium?
Unbinilium, also known as eka-radium or element 120, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubn and atomic number 120.
What is the atomic number of Arsenic?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
In what year did Ted Kaczynski die?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Angelman syndrome discovered?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Yakovlev MC-21: United Aircraft Corporation. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Lynx?
Lynx (constellation): Johannes Hevelius. Lynx is a constellation named after the animal, usually observed in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Newton's law of universal gravitation?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Robert Hooke. This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.
Who is credited with discovering Pulsar?
Pulsar: Jocelyn Bell Burnell. This produces a very precise interval between pulses that ranges from milliseconds to seconds for an individual pulsar.
Who is credited with discovering Coma Berenices?
Coma Berenices: Conon of Samos. Coma Berenices is an ancient asterism in the northern sky, which has been defined as one of the 88 modern constellations.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
Named for the Portuguese word for indigo shrub, this simplest aromatic amine smells of rotten fish, ignites into a smoky flame, and is a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what compound is it?
Aniline (From) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.

Around 1920, when the energy source of stars was a complete mystery, which English astrophysicist boldly and correctly guessed it was the fusion of hydrogen into helium — and lent his name to a natural ceiling on a star's brightness?
Arthur Eddington (28 December 1882 - 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.

An Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean, it is one of two living members of the family Monodontidae and is also known as the white whale (the only cetacean regularly occurring with this color) and the sea canary for its high-pitched calls. What is it?
Beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.

This semi-solid tissue inside the spongy portions of bones serves as the primary site of new blood cell production in birds and mammals, making up roughly 5% of an adult human's body mass — what tissue is it?
Bone marrow is a semi-solid tissue found within the spongy (also known as cancellous) portions of bones.
Its three-dimensional shape mimics adenosine closely enough to plug into the same receptors, blocking the brain's signal to wind down — which psychoactive substance is it?
Caffeine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant of the methylxanthine class and is the most commonly consumed psychoactive substance globally.

A cultivated variety of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this vegetable's edible part is a dense head of undeveloped flower buds called the curd — one variety, Romanesco, grows its curds in stunning fractal spirals. Name this vegetable?
Charted in 1756 by Lacaille and named for the drafting tool that draws circles, this faint southern constellation is easily confused with the mariner's-compass constellation Pyxis. Which one is it?
Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
This inorganic compound's blue crystalline pentahydrate form was historically called blue vitriol, while its anhydrous form is white and dissolves in water to form an octahedral complex. What is it?
Copper(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula CuSO4.
Born at the Point McLeay Mission in 1872, this preacher and inventor who registered 10 patents is widely credited as the first Aboriginal Australian published author — who is he?
David Unaipon was an Aboriginal Australian preacher, inventor, and writer who has been widely credited as the first Aboriginal published author.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.

Often used to keep blood pressure from dropping during anesthesia, this stimulant has also been tried against asthma, obesity, and even narcolepsy — though it's no longer the preferred fix. What is it?
Ephedrine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and sympathomimetic agent that is often used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia.
This type of anaerobic metabolism harnesses the redox potential of reactants like glucose to produce ATP without needing oxygen. What process is it?
Fermentation is a type of anaerobic metabolism that harnesses the redox potential of the reactants to make adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and organic end products.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
In organisms whose total cell count is fixed at maturity, this cell-enlargement process drives nearly all further growth after the embryonic stage — what is it?
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.
This 19th-century French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and his name now sits on a crater on the Moon. Who was he?

Joseph Liouville (24 March 1809 - 8 September 1882) was a French mathematician who worked on a number of different fields in mathematics, including number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally grouped under a nickname referencing marital loss, encompassing both black and brown members — what is its scientific name?
Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
Prized as one of the most profitable seafood commodities in the coastal waters where it's caught, this clawed crustacean spends its life in crevices and burrows on the sea floor - which creature?
Lobster are malacostracan decapod crustaceans of the family Nephropidae or its synonym Homaridae.
Its bell-shaped flowers give way to yellow or orange berries, but this nightshade genus is better known by the folkloric root that inspired countless myths and superstitions — which genus?
Mandragora (genus) is a plant genus belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
These small, non-vascular, flowerless plants form dense green clumps or mats in damp, shady spots — name this group of plants?
Moss are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta sensu stricto.
This form of vitamin B3 is taken orally to treat pellagra without the skin-flushing side effect of niacin, and used as a cream to fight acne and reduce signs of aging skin — what's the compound?
Nicotinamide (INN, BAN UK) or niacinamide (USAN US) (IUPAC name: 3-pyridinecarboxoamide) is a form of vitamin B3 found in food and used as a dietary supplement and medication.
This flowering herb in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean, is sometimes called wild marjoram and is a staple of countless savory dishes. What is it?
Oregano (Origanum vulgare) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
First domesticated in Neolithic China and rarely living past twenty years, this deciduous fruit tree also produces a smooth-skinned variety commercially sold as a different fruit — which tree?
Peach (Prunus persica) is a deciduous tree that bears edible juicy fruits with various characteristics.
Whether captured electronically on a sensor or chemically on light-sensitive film, this art and practice of recording light also powers science and manufacturing — think photolithography. What is it?

Photography is the art, application, and practice of creating images by recording light, either electronically by means of an image sensor, or chemically by means of a light-sensitive material such as photographic film.
This autonomic nervous system disorder causes an abnormally large jump in heart rate — thirty beats per minute within ten minutes — simply from sitting up or standing. What condition is it?
Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a condition characterized by an abnormally large increase in heart rate upon sitting up or standing.
One of America's top rocketry and high-speed-flight experts, this engineer helped found engineering cybernetics before being deported to China in 1955. Who was he?

Qian Xuesen (December 11, 1911 - October 31, 2009; also spelled as Tsien Hsue-shen) was a Chinese aerospace engineer and cyberneticist who made significant contributions to the field of aerodynamics and established engineering cybernetics.
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.
Spanning continents from North America to temperate Asia, this genus covers the majority of the world's common bushy-tailed squirrels — which genus?
Sciurus (or) contains most of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.
Also known as sea stars, roughly 1,900 species of these star-shaped marine invertebrates live on seabeds from warm tropics to icy polar oceans. What are they?
Starfish are a class of marine invertebrates generally shaped like a star polygon.
A staple corm across African, Caribbean, Oceanian, and Asian cultures, this root vegetable of the arum family is often likened to yams — what is it?
Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
Sold under the brand name Xanax, this fast-acting benzodiazepine is most often prescribed for panic disorder and generalized anxiety — what drug is it?
Alprazolam: Benzodiazepine medication. Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of anxiety disorders, especially panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).
Likened to a bubble or balloon, this outward bulge forms at a weak spot in a blood-vessel wall and grows ever more dangerous as it risks rupture — what is it?
Aneurysm: Bulge in the wall of a blood vessel. An aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
Sold under the brand name Strattera, this selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats ADHD and is only recommended for patients age six and up — what is this medication?
Atomoxetine: Medication used to treat ADHD.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Rooted in prehistoric herbalism for identifying edible and medicinal species, this branch of biology studies roughly 410,000 species of land plants — what field of study?
Named from the Greek word for butter, this oily, foul-smelling compound with the formula CH3CH2CH2COOH is a key component of the mammalian gut. What is it?
Butyric acid: Chemical compound (CH3CH2CH2COOH). It is an oily, colorless liquid with an unpleasant odor.
Discovered by a Swiss chemist in 1953 and sold as Tegretol, this anticonvulsant treats epilepsy and neuropathic pain and sits on the WHO's list of essential medicines. Which drug is it?
Carbamazepine: Anticonvulsant medication. Carbamazepine, sold under the brand name Tegretol among others, is an anticonvulsant medication used in the treatment of epilepsy and neuropathic pain.
Every one of these segmented arthropods is venomous, delivering its sting through pincer-like 'legs' rather than fangs — and despite its name, none has exactly 100 of those legs — what is it?
Centipede: Many-legged arthropods with elongated bodies.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.
A tropane alkaloid drawn from the leaves of South American coca plants, it once served doctors as a local anesthetic with handy vasoconstricting properties — what is this stimulant?

Cocaine: Tropane alkaloid and stimulant drug. The leaves are processed into cocaine paste, a crude mixture of coca alkaloids, from which cocaine base is isolated and then converted to cocaine hydrochloride.
This miniature Belgian-French dog breed comes in two varieties named for a butterfly and a moth, based on whether their ears stand erect or hang down — which breed?
Continental Toy Spaniel: Belgian and French breed of dog. The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
First flown in 1938 and built almost 14,000 strong at a factory in Buffalo, New York, this WWII fighter-bomber was known to British and Soviet pilots as the Tomahawk or Kittyhawk — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: American WWII fighter. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Spread by mosquitoes in tropical regions, this virus is often mild but can turn severe with bleeding, plummeting platelet counts, and dangerously low blood pressure — what is it?
A Canadian optical physicist at Waterloo, she shared the 2018 Nobel in Physics for the practical implementation of chirped pulse amplification — who is she?
Donna Strickland: Canadian physicist, engineer, and Nobel laureate.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
Also known as the bodhi tree, this species is revered in four South Asian religions as the tree beneath which Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment — which species?
Ficus religiosa: Species of fig. Ficus religiosa or sacred fig is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?

Germany's first professor of experimental physics is remembered both for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him and for the witty posthumous notebooks he called "waste books" — who was he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg: German scientist and satirist (1742–1799)
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.

Famous for the ideas of "bounded rationality" and "satisficing," this remarkable scholar won both a Turing Award and a Nobel in Economics — bridging computer science, economics, and psychology. Who was he?
Herbert A. Simon: American academic and Nobel Laureate (1916–2001)

Found only in the Americas from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, these roughly 375 species pull off rapid, maneuverable flight thanks to an exceptional metabolism — and their males flaunt the widest plumage diversity of any bird — what are they?
Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'intestinal obstruction,' this medical condition disrupts the gut's normal propulsive movement, whether from lost peristalsis or a physical blockage — what is it?
Ileus: Disruption to the propulsive ability of the intestine.
Nicknamed 'Dr. Death,' this pathologist assisted at least 130 patients in dying and was convicted of murder after broadcasting one such case on television — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian: American pathologist and euthanasia activist (1928–2011)
This physician ran the Battle Creek Sanitarium — part spa, part hospital, part luxury hotel — where he treated the rich and poor alike and devised numerous nut and vegetable products — who is it?
Also called Bushman's tea, the leaves of this East African shrub are chewed as a recreational stimulant, most popular among Somalis and Yemenis — what is it?
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented worms are mostly freshwater dwellers, and the medicinal species famously feeds on blood — what are they?
Leech: Parasitic or predatory annelid worms.
Tucked mostly beneath the right rib cage, this organ detoxifies the body, stores glucose as glycogen, and produces the bile that helps digest fat — which organ?
Liver: Vertebrate organ involved in metabolism.

Originally built at a Boston hospital to manage patient records, this programming language pairs directly with an integrated key-value database and now underpins Epic's electronic health records — which language?
MUMPS: Programming language. It was originally developed at Massachusetts General Hospital for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
Known by the pseudonym 'Notch,' this Swedish programmer created the best-selling video game of all time and became a billionaire when Microsoft bought his studio for $2.5 billion in 2014 — who is he?
Markus Persson: Swedish video game programmer (born 1979)
More than 80% of cases of this cancer — which grows in the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — trace back to asbestos exposure. What is it?
The galaxy containing our Solar System takes its name from how it appears from Earth. What does it look like in the night sky?
The Milky Way is the galaxy that includes the Solar System, with the name describing the galaxy's appearance from Earth: a hazy band of light seen in the night sky.
With a pointed snout, round ears, and a scaly tail as long as its body, this small rodent species is usually distinguished from its larger cousin the rat mainly by size — which animal?
Mouse: Small long-tailed rodent. A mouse (pl. mice) is a small rodent, characteristically known to have a pointed snout, small rounded ears, a body-length scaly tail, and a high breeding rate.
Divided anatomically into vertebral, visceral, and two vascular compartments, which flexible body part connects the head to the torso and is also called the cervix or collum?
Neck: Body part that connects the head and torso. It supports the weight of the head and protects the nerves that transmit sensory and motor information between the brain and the rest of the body.
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
Found on every continent but Antarctica, these flowers can lure pollinators by mimicking female insects, and their tiny seeds depend on fungal partners just to sprout. What plant family is this?
Orchid: Family of flowering plants in the order Asparagales.
This term describes the bulk functional tissue of an organ like the brain or lungs, the filler tissue inside flatworms, and certain leaf cross-section layers in plants — what is it?
Parenchyma: Visceral tissue found inside organs of animals.
In mathematics, what term describes both an ordered arrangement of a set's members and the act of rearranging them, as seen in the six possible orderings of three distinct numbers?
Permutation: Mathematical version of an order change.
Linked to prolonged sitting and excess hair, which skin condition causes a cyst to form between the cheeks of the buttocks and is treated with incision and drainage?
Pilonidal disease: Skin infection between the buttocks. Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Soft enough to slice with a knife, this silvery alkali metal carries the symbol K and takes its name from potash, the plant ashes it was first isolated from — what element is it?
Potassium: Chemical element with atomic number 19 (K)
This emotional response to severe distressing events like violence or a life-threatening injury can trigger flashbacks, panic attacks, insomnia, and post-traumatic stress disorder — what's it called?
Psychological trauma: Emotional response caused by severe distressing events.
This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species includes the buttercups, spearworts, and water crowfoots — which genus?
Ranunculus: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family.
Its seeds yield castor oil but also harbor a highly potent toxin — which plant genus, better known for producing the castor bean?
Ricinus: Monotypic genus of plant in the spurge family.
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?
Blurring the line between a single creature and a colony, this cnidarian is actually made of specialized zooids from one fertilized egg working together to float, feed and jet-propel — what is it?
Siphonophore: Order of colonial hydrozoans with differentiated zooids.
With over 60 types found throughout the human body, this ring-shaped muscle keeps a bodily passage closed until it relaxes to let something through — what is it called?
Sphincter: Circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid made from benzene is the precursor to polystyrene, with global production reaching some 35 million tonnes by 2018 — what compound is it?
Styrene: Chemical compound. Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.
Despite over a thousand species of this large hairy spider, many popular pet varieties defend themselves with irritating urticating hairs rather than a dangerous bite — which arachnid?
Deaf from childhood and largely self-taught, this American began as a railroad telegrapher tinkering with telegraph systems before becoming a legendary inventor — who was he?
Thomas Edison: American inventor and businessman (1847–1931)

Occurring naturally in small amounts in dairy and meat but produced in large quantities by partially hydrogenating vegetable oils, this compound has been banned or tightly regulated in many countries — what is it, chemically speaking?
Trans fat: Type of unsaturated fat.
Element 124, also called eka-uranium, is a hypothetical g-block superactinide that may sit within the "island of stability" — what is its placeholder name?
Unbiquadium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 124 (Ubq)
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
The largest wild member of the dog family, it can still breed fertile hybrids with coyotes and jackals, and counts the domestic dog and dingo among its many subspecies — what animal is it?
The symbol for roentgenium is Rg. Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
The symbol for gold is Au. Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au and atomic number 79.

Cheryl Hines: Cheryl Ruth Hines (born September 21, 1965) is an American actress and comedian.
